answer.answer: The measure counts death from any cause within 30 days of the index hospital admission. records.question: Which interventions make up the SEP-1 numerator, and which patients are excluded?

answer.question: Which interventions make up the SEP-1 numerator, and which patients are excluded?
answer.answer: The numerator includes denominator patients who receive all applicable interventions: initial lactate measurement, blood cultures, antibiotics, fluid resuscitation, repeat lactate, vasopressors, and reassessment of volume status and tissue perfusion. The requirements include initial tests and antibiotics within three hours, and applicable follow-up care within six hours—for example, repeat lactate if the initial level is above 2 mmol/L, and vasopressors or reassessment when specified conditions are present. Exclusions include patients without severe sepsis, those transferred from another acute care facility, those who had received intravenous antibiotics for more than 24 hours before severe sepsis presentation, patients with the specified early comfort-care or administrative contraindications, patients discharged within six hours of presentation, stays longer than 120 days, and clinical-trial participants.
